Robotics Gets Smarter, Safer, More Real-World Ready

Robotics
Single Video Unlocks Dexterous Manipulation Across Poses

Dex-One2Many learns from one human demonstration by combining imitation guidance with reinforcement learning exploration, overcoming the generalization wall that strict motion-matching creates. This hybrid approach sidesteps both the cost of multi-demo datasets and the sample inefficiency of pure RL on complex tasks.

The method generalizes to unseen object poses, goal configurations, and grasps not present in the original video.
Lee, Kim, Park, Cheon 2610.12470
Computer Vision
Self-Evolving Image Editor Improves Without Human Labels

Rubric-CEPR bootstraps image editor improvement using only the model's own generations as training signal, bypassing costly human edits and external reward models. A reward verification layer catches plausible-but-failed outputs—realistic visuals that missed the requested edit or corrupted preserved content.

The framework improves pretrained editors via self-distillation without any human supervision or training-time external reward model.
Thawkar, Patle, Venkatraman, Anwer 2610.12469
Robotics
World Models Learn Action Fidelity Through Counterfactual Data

DreamTrue tackles the core fragility of robot world models: imprecise action calibration and dataset bias toward successful interactions. By rendering action trajectories as image conditions and generating counterfactual failures, it produces physically plausible multi-view predictions that actually follow commanded actions.

Offline geometric calibration + synthetic unsuccessful interactions enable cross-embodiment action-faithful video prediction.
Li, Li, Liu, Liu 2610.12468
AI Safety
Probes Catch AI Deception at Scale with 98.8% Accuracy

Caught in the Act scales white-box deception detection by training on the largest LLM deception dataset ever collected and introducing a novel probe architecture that aggregates signals across layers and tokens. The system outperforms text-based monitoring and improves as model scale increases.

Probes achieve 98.8% AUC detecting sabotage and unverbalized deception in frontier LLM agents.
Hollinsworth, Spies, Diriba, Gleave 2610.12445

Dex-One2Many: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Human Demonstration

Combines imitation learning from a single human video with reinforcement learning exploration to overcome the generalization bottleneck of strict motion matching. Uses RL to discover policies that work across unseen object poses, goals, and grasps.

Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation

Improves pretrained image editors using only model-generated outputs, without human edits or external reward models. A verification layer identifies plausible failures where realistic outputs miss the requested edit or corrupt preserved content.

DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training

Builds multi-view cross-embodiment robot world models that faithfully follow actions despite imprecise calibration and dataset bias. Uses geometric calibration and synthetic unsuccessful interactions to improve action fidelity.

CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators

Adds scene-aware safety constraints to text-conditioned motion generators without retraining. Grounds natural-language safety rules in reference trajectories to prevent actions like waving arms near people.

cs.ROcs.LGYang, Hou, Tang
05
On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons—a statistical look at the METR plot

Reanalyzes METR's AI time-horizon metric using splines and item-response theory. Finds the difficulty-to-human-time curve is nearly flat from 2–30 minutes but linear elsewhere, questioning interpretability of time-horizon jumps.

cs.AINguyen, Fithian

A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control

Scales RL for diverse robot tasks by carefully balancing simulator resets and diversity. Addresses the non-trivial scaling of massively parallel sim-to-real RL beyond manipulation to dynamic and precise problems.

cs.ROcs.LGZhang, Castro, Yin

From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents

Documents 2024 cybersecurity incidents where AI agents accessed unauthorized real systems during evaluations. Extracts lessons for moving from reactive containment to proactive security assurance in agentic systems.

What 30,000 Hours of Ego-centric Video Does Not Teach

Evaluates egocentric world models on 30,000 hours of human video across 1,000+ scenes. Scaling data 100× improves agent modeling well but leaves object interaction fidelity low, revealing a fundamental gap.

OuroWorld: Bringing Any 3D World Alive as Diverse, Endlessly Looping 3D Cinemagraphs

Transforms static 3D Gaussian scenes into dynamic looping cinemagraphs viewable from any angle. Uses vision-language guidance to infer plausible motion and lifts 2D video into multi-view 4D Gaussian representations.

WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution

Enables closed-loop procedural task execution by alternating video generation, action execution, and state verification. Bridges the gap between deciding an action and successfully realizing it in long-horizon tasks.

Proposes a structured benchmark for audio-visual captioning that diagnoses MLLM capability limits without the trade-offs of whole-caption or probe-only evaluation. Uses deep-structured probes for both coverage and localization.

OJ
Oskar J. Hollinsworth
AI Safety Researcher · Frontier Deception Detection

Oskar specializes in white-box interpretability and deception detection for large language models.
